cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Know the Procedure
cards.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This door's lock will need replacing. Nobody touches it until I've checked the mechanism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the hinge. I tighten it every week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we begin with the hinge. Don't skip straight to tightening; show me which part moves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The screw spins in its hole. We'll need a longer one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Longer isn't a specification. Show me the replacement you normally use so I can approve it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 confidently diagnoses a lock; B2 redirects to hinge; A3 corrects repair order and A5 demands a specification while relying on B for the actual replacement.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 redirects A1 component; B4 spinning screw identifies why repeated tightening fails, causing A5 replacement selection request.

relationship.evidence: B2 fixes the hinge routinely and B4 proposes the remedy; A's claim of sole approval contrasts with B's useful competence.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4 solution into another supervised choice rather than acknowledging dependence, sustaining the same game.

specificity.evidence: A1 door problem, B2 hinge and B4 spinning screw are enough to follow the practical investigation.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's longer-isn't-a-specification correction is directed at B4; normally use adds an unnecessary presumption about prior replacements.
